newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish hostages freed, Yemen tells Warsaw.
newsitem.headline: Polish hostages freed, Yemen tells Warsaw.

text.p: Authorities in Yemen have informed Poland that tribesmen there have freed a group of Polish hostages they had been holding since last week, the foreign ministry said on Tuesday.

"Yemen's foreign and interior ministries say they are already free," Przemyslaw Antoniewicz, deputy head of the ministry's press office, told Reuters. He added that Poland's ambassador in Yemen had not yet seen the hostages in person and that the ministry could give no further details.

The tourists -- three men and two women aged between 50 and 64 -- were kidnapped on their way to archaeological sites in eastern Yemen by members of the Al al-Masni tribe in the Khawlan area, about 65 km (40 miles) east of the capital, Sanaa.

On Friday, the tribesmen fired grenades at government troops who had surrounded them, killing three soldiers and wounding five. But throughout the kidnapping officials and diplomats said the hostages' lives were not in danger and the authorities had been negotiating their release.
Yemeni authorities on December 19 freed five Dutch tourists who were briefly held by tribesmen north of Sanaa.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped foreigners to use in bargaining with the authorities often over land or water issues.
